subject: On‑prem peering connector: CSR cadence, DNS ownership, and cert handoff
messages:
From: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@acme-corp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: it-security@acme-corp.com
Date: 2028-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: On‑prem peering: who owns the FQDN / cert for the connector?

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our infra team is starting the network prep for the on‑prem peering connector and we ran into a few handoff questions around TLS and DNS that we wanted to lock down before provisioning: 

- Do you expect Redwood to generate the CSR and provide a signed cert for the connector, or does Acme provide its own cert (we manage keys)?
- If Acme owns the private zone, what DNS proof do you need from us for the FQDN (NS delegation, TXT validation, or a zone file snapshot)?
- Rotation cadence: our security policy requires cert rotation every 90 days for ephemeral connectors — are we able to automate CSR renewals with your connector tooling?

We can share our internal DNS ACL and have the security team join if helpful. Attaching our initial checklist.

Appreciate a short call to finalize.

Best,
Sara
Sara Thompson
Senior Cloud Security Engineer, Acme Corporation

Attachments: acme-onprem-checklist.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem peering: who owns the FQDN / cert for the connector?

Sara — thanks for the clear questions. TL;DR: we support both flows but recommend Acme‑managed private zone + customer‑provided cert uploaded to your KMS for strongest separation. Proposed handoff: 

1) DNS ownership: Acme maintains the private hosted zone. You can either (a) delegate a subzone to Redwood by providing NS records, or (b) provide a TXT proof and we’ll accept short lived ACME TXT validation for initial provisioning. We prefer NS delegation for long lived endpoints.

2) Cert flow: two supported patterns:
  - Customer‑owned certs: you issue a cert from your PKI and upload it to your KMS; Redwood will reference it for the connector. This gives you key custody.
  - Redwood‑issued cert: if you prefer Redwood manages issuance, we will generate a CSR and require an out‑of‑band proof (NS or signed CSR response). Certificate TTL and rotation cadence are configurable; we recommend 90 days max if your policy requires it.

3) Automation: we can run an automated CSR renewal pipeline if you allow a short‑lived accept token (rotating secret pinned in your KMS or via our private control plane). If you use customer‑owned certs, rotation is handled by your tooling and Redwood will pick up new versions via the KMS integration webhook.

I’m attaching a one‑page "connector CSR process" diagram and a proposed delegation matrix for responsibilities. Suggest a 30‑minute workshop with your infra + security next Tue.

Next steps (simple):
- Confirm which cert flow you want (Customer KMS vs Redwood issuance)
- If Customer KMS: share the KMS integration owner + permissions
- If Redwood issuance: provide NS delegation or TXT proof per the attached matrix

Happy to jump on a screen share to walk through.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: connector-csr-process.pdf (attachment stub), delegation-matrix.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-03T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem peering: who owns the FQDN / cert for the connector?

Marcus / Laura — quick technical notes to surface before the workshop, based on Acme's note about 90‑day rotations: 

- SAN vs wildcard: for peered connectors we strongly prefer explicit SANs (single FQDN per connector). Wildcards complicate audit and make pinning harder for clients in air‑gapped networks.
- Split‑horizon DNS: if Acme uses internal resolution, NS delegation needs to be visible from their VPC/resolver path. If they cannot delegate, the TXT ACME method is acceptable but it requires us to cache validation state and extend monitoring.
- OCSP/CRL considerations: we should agree whether OCSP stapling will be used for the customer‑owned cert path; many enterprise PKIs disable stapling. We need to capture that in the delegation matrix.

Also, small ops ask: if they want Redwood to rotate certs, we need an SLA addendum for rotation windows and an emergency rollback key for immediate replace. Happy to draft the minimal addendum.

—Priyom
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-05T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem peering: who owns the FQDN / cert for the connector?

Sara — following internal alignment, here is our recommended, low‑risk plan and the minimal paperwork we need to proceed. I’ve annotated the delegation matrix and attached an SOW draft (DocuSign link below).

Recommended default (for compliance and key custody):
- Acme owns the private hosted zone. You delegate a subdomain to Redwood by providing NS records for the connector host. Example: connector-01.acme.internal -> delegation to ns1.redwood-peering.internal
- Acme provides a certificate issued by your PKI and stores the private key in your KMS/HSM. Redwood will reference the cert by ARN and will never have key material.
- Rotation: Acme rotates certs at 90‑day cadence. Redwood will pick up new cert versions via the KMS webhook and perform a zero‑downtime swap during the configured maintenance window.

Fallback (if delegation not possible):
- Use ACME TXT validation for initial provisioning. This requires a short‑lived one‑time token we validate and then discard. Renewal automation possible but will require periodic proof (every N days) depending on your DNS TTLs.

Operational asks from Acme:
- Confirm subdomain string to delegate (we recommend prefixing with "connector-<region>-<env>")
- Provide a KMS integration owner + minimal read/list permissions for cert metadata
- Confirm OCSP stapling expectations (yes/no)

Paperwork / links: 
- SOW draft (for Managed Rotation option): https://docusign.com/packets/ACME-Redwood-Onprem-SOW-2028
- Internal playbook (read‑only): https://redwood-internal.drive/Shared/Onprem-Connector-Playbook

Attachments: sow-onprem-connector.docx (attachment stub)

If that plan looks good, can we run the workshop on Tue 2028-11-07 10:00am PT? I’ll bring Ops and the cert automation engineer.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
